title: Duplicate tool invocations after edge reconnect and proxy replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported duplicated tool/function callbacks and repeated structured outputs when an edge proxy reconnect or transient network replay occurred. The duplicates manifest as repeated 'invoke' events sent to downstream tool adapters (webhooks/third-party connectors) resulting in duplicate side-effects (double charges, duplicate messages). Issue spans Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments depending on whether edge proxies or customer-side proxies performed short reconnects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a streaming generation session that triggers a tool/function call mid-stream (function call enabled and streaming=true).

2) Simulate a transient network interruption between the edge proxy and runtime (TCP RST or short disconnect) during the portion of the stream where the runtime emits the tool-call envelope, then allow proxy to reconnect and replay buffered segments.

3) Observe downstream tool adapter receives two separate invoke POSTs for the same logical invocation id and same payload, sometimes with slightly shifted byte offsets in the structured output envelope.
4) Reproduce reliably by enabling retry-on-reconnect at proxy + buffered-replay mode (seen in customer appliances and older public proxies).
observed_behavior: Downstream adapters receive duplicate callback HTTP requests with identical payloads or semantically identical structured outputs. On some customers we saw a second callback with truncated trailing bytes which the adapter interprets as a new invocation. In others, dedupe behaved correctly because adapters used idempotency keys. Root cause appears to be mismatched session/invocation tagging combined with proxy-level chunk replay and our streaming envelope resynchronization logic failing to detect already-delivered envelopes.
root_cause: Edge/proxy replay can cause the runtime to re-emit tool-call envelopes when a reconnect triggers a resynchronization path. The runtime's streaming envelope parser uses an in-memory session tag to dedupe only within a single connection; reconnects create new session contexts and the invocation_id was not persisted to the connection-resume handshake, so replayed buffer results in duplicate delivery. Additionally, certain byte-shifted envelope fragments caused the downstream parser to treat repeats as new invocations.
proposed_solution: 1) Short-term mitigation: server-side duplicate detection: persist recent invocation_id -> terminal-state for a short TTL (30s) in a shared cache (Redis) and reject duplicate invokes with 409 to adapters. 2) Medium-term: include connection-resume idempotency token in the reconnect handshake and rehydrate per-session seen-invocations set; ensure replayed buffers are compared against invocation IDs rather than connection-local sequence numbers. 3) Parser hardening: normalize envelope boundary handling to tolerate byte shifts and merge adjacent fragments deterministically.
implementation_notes: - Add small LRU cache keyed by (tenant_id, invocation_id) with configurable TTL; store terminal status (delivered/acknowledged).
- Extend edge protocol: add 'resume_token' that is returned by runtime on connection and must be supplied by proxy on reconnect to reattach session metadata.
- Update streaming parser to canonicalize whitespace/control characters at fragment joins and validate complete JSON tool payload before emitting invoke event.
- New config flags: enable_replay_dedupe (opt-in per-customer) for initial rollout to avoid unexpected behavior in very old proxies.
- Backwards compatibility: proxies that do not support resume_token continue to work; dedupe cache provides protection but with TTL limitations.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix): Deploy dedupe cache to runtime staging and toggle on for affected customers only. Monitor adapter 409 rates and customer symptom reduction.
Phase 1 (canary): Release resume_token handshake and parser fixes to canary fleet, enable for low-traffic tenants and Dedicated hosts with support engineers standing by.
Phase 2 (gradual): Ramp to all hosted regions and offer a Private/Dedicated upgrade package. Coordinate with customer SREs for upgrades on private appliances.
Phase 3 (cleanup): Deprecate old replay-prone proxy behaviors and remove opt-in flag after 6 weeks of stable telemetry.
Rollback: Revert resume_token changes if unexpected client compatibility errors exceed threshold; fallback will keep dedupe cache enabled.
test_plan: Unit tests for dedupe cache eviction and collision behavior.
Integration tests simulating proxy reconnect + buffered replay ensuring single invoke delivered.
Fuzz tests for fragment boundary shifts and random byte offsets to verify parser normalization.
End-to-end tests against a mock downstream adapter verifying idempotent 200/409 semantics.
Customer validation: coordinated upgrade with 3 reporting customers (AcmePayments, MedNotify, ChatFlow) to confirm no duplicate side-effects.
monitoring_and_metrics: Metric: invoke_409_rejected_count (adapters responding with 409 due to dedupe)
Alert: duplicate_invoke_rate > 0.1% for 10m for a tenant => Pager P1
Dashboard: per-tenant streaming-session-resume success rate and average resume_token roundtrip latency
Post-deploy runbook: how to temporarily opt a tenant out by toggling enable_replay_dedupe=false
